questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Any glad hand can connect to any other glad hand.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: Always connect matching glad hands. They are color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: If a vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in a collision, the driver should:

options.text: Not warn others about the danger.
Keep the explosives in the vehicle until the vehicles are separated.
Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating it from the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating it from the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives is in an accident, warn others, keep people away, and do not allow smoking or open fires. Remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any occupied buildings.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?

options.text: Between three-quarters of a second and one second

questions.correctAnswerText: Between three-quarters of a second and one second
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between three-quarters of a second and one second.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, how far ahead can you see?
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. When driving at night, adjust your speed so you can stop within the lit area ahead.

questions.question: Where should the identification number for a hazardous material appear?
questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the shipping papers and packaging. It must also appear on cargo tanks and bulk containers.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: On combination vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer develops a leak or breaks away.

questions.question: How must placards be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: Any way, as long as they are visible.
So words and numbers read from left to right.
Within three inches of other markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed so words and numbers can be read from left to right. They must be at least three inches away from other markings.

questions.question: What is the service air line attached to?
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It is attached to relay valves, which allow trailer brakes to apply quickly.

questions.question: What emergency equipment must a commercial vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if carrying hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged and rated fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When can mirror adjustment be checked properly?

options.text: When there is no trailer attached.
When the vehicle is on a slight incline.
When the vehicle is on a slight decline.

questions.explanation: If a trailer is attached, mirrors can only be checked accurately when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: When driving a heavy vehicle, how should you avoid blocking traffic?

options.text: Pass other vehicles while going uphill.
Use the brakes while going downhill.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle is too heavy to match the speed of other traffic, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: Unbaffled tanks are also called ____ tanks.
questions.explanation: Unbaffled tanks are also called smooth bore tanks.

questions.question: What can affect how far it takes your vehicle to stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by how fast you are driving, your vehicle's weight, and how slippery the road surface is.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while double clutching and cannot shift to the next gear, what should you do?

options.text: Stop the vehicle and start over.
Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
Skip your intended gear and shift to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long while double clutching and have trouble shifting, do not force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: When passing a bicycle, you must leave at least ____ of space between your vehicle and the bicycle.
questions.explanation: You must keep at least four feet between your vehicle and a bicycle when passing. You may cross a double yellow line if needed to keep this distance safe.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer, what should you do next?
questions.explanation: After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer. Following the correct steps to couple trailers is important for safe driving.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A construction worker near the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful near people who are not paying attention to traffic. Watch out for road workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road.

questions.question: When checking the engine, what should you do?

options.text: Do not engage the parking brake.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine, turn on the parking brake and/or chock the wheels. Check the engine before you get in the cab and start it.

questions.question: When using controlled braking with liquid cargo, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brakes with about half your usual force.
Apply the brakes until the wheels lock.
Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Apply the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep small steering movements when braking this way.

questions.question: When you see a construction worker near the road, what should you do?

options.text: Do not drive in any lane.
Wait until construction is complete before driving.

questions.explanation: In work zones with workers on or near the road, reduce your speed.
